1	//! Router construction for both API surfaces.
2	//!
3	//! Two separate routers are built:
4	//! - [`build_native_router`] — mounted on `:8080`, native xerj API.
5	//! - [`build_es_compat_router`] — mounted on `:9200`, ES-compatible API.
6	//!
7	//! Both routers share the same [`AppState`] instance via `Arc`. Common
8	//! middleware (request-ID injection, per-request tracing, CORS) is applied
9	//! to both.
10	
11	use axum::{
12	    extract::{DefaultBodyLimit, Request, State},
13	    http::{HeaderValue, Method},
14	    middleware::{self, Next},
15	    response::{IntoResponse, Response},
16	    routing::{delete, get, post, put},
17	    Router,
18	};
19	use tower_http::{
20	    classify::{ServerErrorsAsFailures, SharedClassifier},
21	    cors::{AllowOrigin, Any, CorsLayer},
22	    decompression::RequestDecompressionLayer,
23	    limit::RequestBodyLimitLayer,
24	    trace::{DefaultMakeSpan, DefaultOnRequest, DefaultOnResponse, TraceLayer},
25	};
26	use tracing::Level;
27	use uuid::Uuid;
28	use xerj_common::config::CorsConfig;
29	
30	use crate::{
31	    ask_api, audit_mw, auth::auth_middleware, authz, es_compat, graph_api, ism_api, memory_api,
32	    native, share, state::AppState, systemone_api, wal_tap_api,
33	};
34	
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	// Native xerj router (:8080)
37	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	
39	/// Build the native xerj router.
40	///
41	/// Routes:
42	/// ```text
43	/// POST   /v1/indices                        create_index
44	/// GET    /v1/indices/:name                  get_index
45	/// DELETE /v1/indices/:name                  delete_index
46	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/docs             ingest_docs
47	/// GET    /v1/indices/:name/docs/:id         get_doc
48	/// DELETE /v1/indices/:name/docs/:id         delete_doc
49	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/docs/_bulk       bulk_ingest
50	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/turbo-ingest     turbo_ingest (opt-in high-throughput)
51	/// GET    /v1/indices/:name/encodings        get_index_encodings (per-field compression stats)
52	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/search           search
53	/// POST   /v1/indices/:name/_flush           flush_index
54	/// GET    /v1/health                         health
55	/// GET    /v1/health/ready                   readiness probe (200 unless nothing can be served)
56	/// GET    /v1/cluster/health                 cluster_health
57	/// GET    /_cluster/indices/failed           failed_indices (name + open error)
58	/// POST   /_cluster/indices/failed/:name/_retry  retry_failed_index
59	/// POST   /v1/admin/flush                    admin_flush (flush all indices)
60	/// POST   /v1/admin/backup                   admin_backup (snapshot to disk)
61	/// GET    /v1/metrics                        metrics (Prometheus text)
62	/// GET    /v1/schema/:name                   get_schema
63	/// POST   /v1/schema/:name/evolve            evolve_schema
64	/// ```
65	pub fn build_native_router(state: AppState) -> Router {
66	    let body_limit = state.config.limits.max_body_bytes;
67	    let access_log = state.config.logging.access_log;
68	    // Build the CORS layer before `state` is moved into the auth middleware.
69	    let cors = cors_layer(&state.config.cors);
70	    // Note: this router does NOT serve `/_xerj-console/*` — that namespace is
71	    // owned by the `xerj-console-api` crate, mounted by `xerj-server` as a
72	    // peer router via `Router::merge`. Engine API and Xerj Console API are
73	    // independent surfaces sharing one TCP listener.
74	    Router::new()
75	        // Index management
76	        .route("/v1/indices", post(native::create_index))
77	        .route(
78	            "/v1/indices/:name",
79	            get(native::get_index).delete(native::delete_index),
80	        )
81	        // Document operations
82	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/docs", post(native::ingest_docs))
83	        .route(
84	            "/v1/indices/:name/docs/:id",
85	            get(native::get_doc).delete(native::delete_doc),
86	        )
87	        // Bulk ingest
88	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/docs/_bulk", post(native::bulk_ingest))
89	        // Turbo ingest — high-throughput batched parallel ingest (opt-in)
90	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/turbo-ingest", post(native::turbo_ingest))
91	        // Log ingest (auto-ID for every record)
92	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/logs", post(native::ingest_logs))
93	        // OTLP log ingest (OpenTelemetry JSON format)
94	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/otlp", post(native::ingest_otlp))
95	        // Syslog ingest (RFC 5424 / RFC 3164 plain-text lines)
96	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/syslog", post(native::ingest_syslog))
97	        // Search
98	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/search", post(native::search))
99	        // Per-field smart encoding analysis
100	        .route(
101	            "/v1/indices/:name/encodings",
102	            get(native::get_index_encodings),
103	        )
104	        // Flush memtable to durable segment
105	        .route("/v1/indices/:name/_flush", post(native::flush_index))
106	        // Cluster / observability
107	        .route("/v1/health", get(native::health))
108	        .route("/v1/health/ready", get(native::readiness))
109	        .route("/v1/cluster/health", get(native::cluster_health))
110	        // Failed-index recovery (issue #206) — inspect / retry. Delete goes
111	        // through the ordinary `DELETE /{index}`. Mounted on both routers
112	        // under the same path so an operator does not have to know which
113	        // listener they reached.
114	        .route("/_cluster/indices/failed", get(native::failed_indices))
115	        .route(
116	            "/_cluster/indices/failed/:name/_retry",
117	            post(native::retry_failed_index),
118	        )
119	        .route(
120	            "/v1/embedding/identity",
121	            get(native::embedding_execution_identity),
122	        )
123	        // k8s probes — v0.8 8-P4 — see comment in `native.rs::liveness`.
124	        .route("/health/live", get(native::liveness))
125	        .route("/health/ready", get(native::readiness))

1012	        resp

1043	/// Middleware that sets ES-compatible product headers on every response.
1044	///
1045	/// Kibana and other Elastic clients verify the presence of `X-Elastic-Product`
1046	/// before trusting the response. A real OpenSearch server never sends this
1047	/// header at all, so a caller detected (or forced, see
1048	/// [`es_compat::is_opensearch_caller`]) as OpenSearch must NOT receive it —
1049	/// some OpenSearch-ecosystem clients treat an unexpected product header as
1050	/// just another response header, but there's no reason to send an
1051	/// Elastic-specific identity marker to a client we've already decided isn't
1052	/// Elastic. A `Warning` header is included for Elastic callers only, for the
1053	/// same reason.
1054	///
1055	/// A real OpenSearch server also sends `X-OpenSearch-Version: OpenSearch/<n>
1056	/// (opensearch)` on every response, verified against a real OpenSearch 3.7.0
1057	/// container — an OpenSearch-detected caller gets the equivalent header
1058	/// here, built from the same version xerj already reports in `GET /`'s
1059	/// `version` block (`es_compat::resolve_compat_version`), so the two stay in
1060	/// sync by construction. Found missing while chasing an OpenSearch
1061	/// Dashboards Timeline (Timelion) panel that rendered empty against xerj but
1062	/// correctly against real OpenSearch for the byte-identical aggregation
1063	/// response body — this header was the one structural difference between
1064	/// the two.
1065	async fn es_headers_middleware(
1066	    State(state): State<AppState>,
1067	    req: Request,
1068	    next: Next,
1069	) -> Response {
1070	    let is_opensearch = es_compat::is_opensearch_caller(&state, req.headers());
1071	    let opensearch_version =
1072	        is_opensearch.then(|| es_compat::resolve_compat_version(&state, req.headers()).number);
1073	    let mut resp = next.run(req).await;
1074	    let headers = resp.headers_mut();
1075	    if is_opensearch {
1076	        headers.remove("x-elastic-product");
1077	        headers.remove("warning");
1078	        if let Some(number) = opensearch_version {
1079	            if let Ok(v) = HeaderValue::from_str(&format!("OpenSearch/{number} (opensearch)")) {
1080	                headers.insert("x-opensearch-version", v);
1081	            }
1082	        }
1083	    } else {
1084	        headers.insert(
1085	            "x-elastic-product",
1086	            HeaderValue::from_static("Elasticsearch"),
1087	        );
1088	        // RFC 7234 warning header — signals no specific deprecation for now.
1089	        if let Ok(v) = HeaderValue::from_str("299 Elasticsearch-8.13.0 \"\"") {
1090	            headers.insert("warning", v);
1091	        }
1092	    }
1093	    resp
1094	}

# SECURITY AUDIT — INGEST OF UNTRUSTED DOCUMENTS (XERJ)

**Threat model:** malicious document author / malicious corpus provider. Verified statically against `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine`. Line numbers confirmed on-disk. The highest-impact finding on each side was reproduced empirically.

**Universal amplifier:** `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/Cargo.toml:165` — `panic = "abort"` in the release profile. There is no `CatchPanic` layer or `catch_unwind` anywhere on the HTTP ingest path (grep across all crates confirms). **Every panic below is a whole-process kill, not a 500.**

**Default posture is unauthenticated:** `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/auth.rs:262-265` returns `Principal::Superuser` in open mode, so the ES-compat ingest API (and pipeline definition) is reachable by any network peer.

## PART A — PIPELINE PROCESSORS / INDEX-TIME INGEST

### A1. CRITICAL — Remote process abort: non-object document root + `set`/`add_field` processor

**`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-wasm/src/builtins.rs:285`** and **`:870`**
```rust

        doc[&self.field] = self.value.clone();      // AddFieldPlugin, :285
```
```rust
        if self.override_existing || !exists {
            doc[&self.field] = self.value.clone();  // SetPlugin, :870
```

`serde_json`'s `IndexMut<&str>` panics on any root that is not `Object` or `Null`. Verified in the locked dependency `serde_json-1.0.149/src/value/index.rs:102`: `_ => panic!("cannot access key {:?} in JSON {}", self, Type(v))`. Reached for `Value::Array`, `String`, `Number`, `Bool`.

These are the **only two** unguarded `doc[&str] =` sites in the crate. Every other one is protected by a preceding `doc.get(&self.field)` probe that returns `None` on a non-object root and short-circuits to `Pass` (`:60-68`, `:117-132`, `:628-630`, `:724-728`, `:762-771`), and `AppendPlugin`/`RemoveNullPlugin` correctly use `as_object_mut()` (`:913-916`, `:955-958`).

`SetPlugin` is strictly worse than `AddFieldPlugin`: `doc.get()` on a non-object returns `None` → `exists = false` → `override_existing || !exists` is unconditionally true, so it **always** writes.

**Reachability (verified end to end).** Four entry points feed an unchecked `Value` into `process_through_pipeline` → `Pipeline::process_batch` (`pipeline.rs:259`: `docs.iter_mut().map(|doc| self.process(doc))`) → the plugin, with no panic boundary:

| Entry point | File:line | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /{index}/_doc` (`index_doc_auto`) | `xerj-api/src/es_compat.rs:2752`, pipeline at `:2810` | parses raw body to `Value`, no shape check |
| `PUT/POST /{index}/_doc/{id}` (`index_doc`) | `es_compat.rs:2888`, pipeline at `:2946` | `Json(doc): Json<Value>` |
| `PUT /{index}/_create/{id}` (`create_doc`) | `es_compat.rs:3068`, pipeline at `:3077` | **zero** validation before pipeline |
| `_bulk` `create` action | `xerj-engine/src/bulk.rs:856`, dispatch at `:1779-1782` | see A2 |


**Trigger processor is client-definable.** Pipelines are writable over HTTP at `router.rs:171` (`PUT /v1/pipelines/:name`) and `router.rs:484` (`PUT /_ingest/pipeline/:id`). The ES `set` processor maps directly onto the vulnerable stage (`es_compat.rs:28888`: `"set" => "set".to_string()`), and the ES→xerj translation **defaults `override` to true** (`es_compat.rs:29272`):
```rust

```

**`/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/es_compat.rs:39145-39149`**

## PART B — AUTOINDEX HOSTILE-FILE PARSING

### B1. CRITICAL — YAML alias bomb in the sniff parse tier: 7 KB file → 17.85 GiB RSS (reproduced)
